structure.title: Preamble and Part I · Give a frightening name a history
structure.text: Marx and Engels open with the panic attached to the word communist, then turn to the achievements of the bourgeoisie. The class they attack has remade cities, distances and daily needs. Its appetite for change gives the account much of its speed.

structure.title: Part II · Answer the accusations
structure.text: Questions about property, family and nationality give the writers imaginary opponents. Their replies repeatedly ask whose property or family arrangement is being defended when an opponent invokes an institution as though it had always had one form.

structure.title: Parts III–IV · Locate the quarrel inside the opposition
structure.text: Rival socialist writings receive pointed portraits before the manifesto turns to political alliances. A reader expecting one united camp against capitalism encounters competing accounts of what was lost, who should act and which future is worth pursuing.

people.name: Bourgeoisie
people.role: Owners who organise production for a market
people.text: The writers credit this class with dissolving old dependencies and producing goods on an extraordinary scale. Their attack gains force from the claim that the same productive powers periodically exceed what their owners can control.

people.name: Proletariat
people.text: Factory production brings workers together while competition sets them against one another. The account of political organisation turns on how people who experience those pressures as individuals could come to recognise a common interest.

context.title: A programme published in 1848
context.text: The work seeks adherents in a Europe of censorship, industrial change and political agitation. Its diagnoses, predictions and demands have different claims on a reader. A confident future tense is part of its attempt to organise action.

notice.text: Watch praise do the work of criticism.
notice.why: The dazzling passage on bourgeois achievement can sound like a hymn to invention. Its very momentum prepares the charge that a social order committed to perpetual upheaval cannot guarantee its own stability.

notice.text: Listen to the voice assigned to an opponent.
notice.why: An objection sometimes arrives already phrased in a way favourable to its answer. Hearing the two voices separately makes it possible to assess both the reply and the fairness of the challenge.

opening: Factories are transforming work, commerce reaches across the world, and arrangements that once seemed permanent are being swept away. Marx and Engels describe this upheaval with an admiration for capitalism's force that can surprise readers expecting only denunciation. Then they argue that the same system is producing the people who will overthrow it. This short declaration gives economic conflict the urgency of a historical showdown, making a case whose extraordinary political afterlife began with the claim that workers could recognise their common situation and act together.
